This is the correct answer. PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique used to transform a set of correlated variables into a smaller set of uncorrelated variables called principal components. [26]
SVM is a supervised learning algorithm for classification and regression. [17]
A decision tree is a supervised learning algorithm used for both classification and regression.
Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classifier based on Bayes' theorem.
questions.explanation: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is the most suitable technique for this purpose. It is a statistical procedure that uses an orthogonal transformation to convert a set of observations of possibly correlated variables into a set of linearly uncorrelated variables called principal components. This is often used for dimensionality reduction and to address multicollinearity in a dataset. [26]

questions.question: A programmer needs to implement a function that sorts a small array of integers that is already nearly sorted. Which sorting algorithm would be the most efficient in this specific scenario due to its adaptive nature?
feedbacks: Quick Sort has an average time complexity of O(n log n) but a worst-case of O(n^2), which can occur if the array is nearly sorted and a poor pivot is chosen. [42]
Merge Sort has a consistent time complexity of O(n log n) but is not adaptive and has higher overhead than simpler algorithms for small inputs. [42]
Heap Sort also has a time complexity of O(n log n) but is not adaptive to the existing order of the elements.
This is the correct answer. Insertion Sort has a time complexity of O(n) in the best case (when the array is already sorted) and performs very well on nearly sorted data. [42]
Selection Sort has a time complexity of O(n^2) regardless of the initial order of the elements.
Bubble Sort can be optimized to have O(n) complexity for nearly sorted data, but Insertion Sort is generally considered more efficient in practice. [42]
questions.explanation: Insertion Sort is the most efficient choice for sorting a small, nearly sorted array. Its time complexity is O(n*k) where n is the number of elements and k is the maximum distance an element is from its sorted position. For nearly sorted data, k is small, and the performance of Insertion Sort approaches O(n), making it faster than more complex algorithms like Quick Sort or Merge Sort in this specific situation. [42]

questions.question: A small company wants to move its IT infrastructure to the cloud. PaaS provides a platform for development but abstracts away the underlying servers and storage, offering less control than IaaS. [2, 6, 8, 9]
This is the correct answer. IaaS provides access to fundamental resources like virtual servers, storage, and networking, offering the most control over the cloud environment. [2, 6, 8, 9]
FaaS is a serverless model that abstracts even more of the infrastructure than PaaS. [5]
DaaS provides data on demand to users, regardless of geographic or organizational separation of provider and consumer.
XaaS is a general, catch-all term for cloud computing services and is not a specific service model.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is the most suitable cloud service model for this company. IaaS provides the fundamental computing, networking, and storage resources on-demand, over the internet, and on a pay-as-you-go basis. questions.question: A process in an operating system is in a state where it is waiting for an I/O operation to complete. In which state is the process?
feedbacks: The 'New' state is when the process is being created. [19]
The 'Ready' state is when the process is waiting to be assigned to a processor. [19]
The 'Running' state is when instructions are being executed. [19]
This is the correct answer. A process enters the Waiting state when it needs to wait for some event to occur, such as the completion of an I/O request. [19]
The 'Terminated' state is when the process has finished execution.
The 'Suspended' state is when a process is temporarily swapped out of main memory.
questions.explanation: When a process is waiting for an I/O operation to complete, it is in the 'Waiting' (or 'Blocked') state. In this state, the process cannot proceed until the I/O device finishes its task and signals the operating system with an interrupt. Once the event has occurred, the process will transition back to the 'Ready' state, waiting for its turn to be executed by the CPU. [19]

questions.question: A system is designed to handle flight reservations. To prevent two travel agents from booking the same seat simultaneously, the system needs to ensure that the seat booking operation is treated as a single, indivisible unit. Which database property ensures this behavior?
feedbacks: This is the correct answer. Atomicity ensures that all operations within a transaction are completed successfully; otherwise, the transaction is aborted, and the database is left unchanged. [34]
Consistency ensures that a transaction brings the database from one valid state to another. [34]
Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. While related, Atomicity is the property that makes the operation indivisible. [34]
Durability ensures that once a transaction has been committed, it will remain so, even in the event of a power loss or crash. [34]
Scalability is the ability of a system to handle a growing amount of work.
Redundancy involves storing data in multiple places to ensure its availability.
questions.explanation: Atomicity is the ACID property that guarantees that a transaction is treated as a single, indivisible unit of work. For the flight reservation system, this means the entire process of checking seat availability, selecting the seat, and confirming the booking must either complete in its entirety or not happen at all. This prevents partial updates and ensures data integrity, making it impossible for two agents to book the same seat. [34]

questions.question: A developer is implementing a feature to export a report in different formats, such as PDF and CSV. The core report generation logic is the same, but the final step of formatting the output is different for each format. The developer wants to define a skeleton of the algorithm in a base class but let subclasses override specific steps. Which behavioral design pattern is best for this?
feedbacks: The Strategy pattern would involve defining a family of algorithms and making them interchangeable, which is a good alternative, but Template Method is better for defining a fixed skeleton. [7]
The Observer pattern is used for notifying dependents of state changes.
This is the correct answer. The Template Method pattern defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a method, deferring some steps to subclasses. [3, 7]
The State pattern allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes.
The Command pattern encapsulates a request as an object.
The Memento pattern is used to capture and restore an object's internal state. [7]
questions.explanation: The Template Method pattern is the most suitable choice for this scenario. It allows you to define the outline of an algorithm in a base class and let subclasses redefine certain steps of the algorithm without changing the algorithm's structure. In this case, the base class would define the overall report generation process, and concrete subclasses would implement the specific formatting for PDF and CSV. [3, 7]

questions.question: A team is working on a project where the requirements are not fully understood at the beginning and are expected to evolve. The Spiral model is an iterative, risk-driven model that would also be appropriate for a project with unclear requirements.
The V-Model is a sequential model and lacks the flexibility needed for this scenario.
Scrum is a specific Agile framework that uses iterative cycles called sprints, making it a very good fit.

questions.question: An attacker gains access to a web server and modifies a popular JavaScript library used by the website to include malicious code. This code then steals session cookies from users who visit the website and sends them to the attacker's server. What is this type of attack called?
feedbacks: SQL Injection targets the database by injecting malicious SQL code. [10, 16]
This is the correct answer. XSS involves injecting malicious scripts into trusted websites, which are then executed in the browsers of unsuspecting users. [18]
A DoS attack aims to make a service unavailable. [12]
Phishing involves tricking users into revealing sensitive information through deceptive emails or websites. [10, 16]
A MitM attack involves intercepting communication between two parties. [18]
A Directory Traversal attack aims to access files and directories stored outside the web root folder.
questions.explanation: This is a classic example of a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack. Specifically, it's a stored XSS attack because the malicious script is permanently stored on the target server (in the modified JavaScript library). When a user's browser loads the compromised page, the malicious script executes, allowing the attacker to steal sensitive information like session cookies. [18]

questions.question: A company needs to transmit a large file reliably over an unreliable network. The file must be received without any errors and in the correct order. Which transport layer protocol should be used for this task?
feedbacks: UDP is a connectionless protocol that prioritizes speed over reliability and does not guarantee delivery or order. [1, 11, 24, 35]
This is the correct answer. TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that provides reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of bytes. [1, 21, 24]
IP is a network layer protocol responsible for addressing and routing, not reliable transport.
HTTP is an application layer protocol that typically uses TCP for its transport. The question asks for the transport layer protocol.
ICMP is used for sending error messages and operational information, not for transferring large files.
ARP is used to resolve an IP address to a MAC address.
questions.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is the appropriate choice for this task. It is designed to provide a reliable, connection-oriented communication service. TCP ensures that all data is delivered in the correct order and without errors by using mechanisms like sequence numbers, acknowledgments, and retransmissions of lost packets. This makes it ideal for applications like file transfer where data integrity is critical. [1, 21, 24]

questions.question: A web browser needs to implement a 'back' button to allow users to navigate to the previously visited page. Which data structure is most suitable for storing the browsing history for this functionality?
feedbacks: A queue uses a FIFO (First-In, First-Out) order, which would be suitable for a 'forward' button but not for a 'back' button. [15]
This is the correct answer. A stack uses a LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) order, so the last page visited is the first one to be retrieved when the 'back' button is clicked. [4, 23]
A hash table is used for fast key-value lookups and does not maintain the sequential order of visited pages.
A tree could represent a complex browsing history with branching paths, but a simple linear 'back' functionality is best served by a stack.
While a stack can be implemented with a linked list, the abstract data type 'stack' with its LIFO operations is the conceptually correct answer.
An array can be used to implement a stack, but the stack itself is the appropriate data structure, not the underlying implementation.
questions.explanation: A stack is the ideal data structure for implementing the 'back' button in a web browser. Because a stack follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle, the most recently visited page is placed on top of the stack. When the user clicks the 'back' button, this page is popped off the stack, revealing the previously visited page. [4, 23]

questions.question: A developer is building a navigation application that needs to find the shortest route between two points in a city, where the roads are represented as a weighted graph (weights represent travel time). Which algorithm is the most appropriate for this task, assuming all travel times are positive?
feedbacks: DFS is a graph traversal algorithm but does not guarantee finding the shortest path in a weighted graph.
BFS can find the shortest path in an unweighted graph, but it is not suitable for weighted graphs. [41]
This is the correct answer. Dijkstra's algorithm is designed to find the shortest path between nodes in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. [41]
Kruskal's algorithm is used to find the minimum spanning tree of a graph, not the shortest path between two points. [41]
Prim's algorithm is also used to find a minimum spanning tree, not the shortest path. [41]
The Bellman-Ford algorithm can handle negative edge weights, but Dijkstra's is generally more efficient for graphs with only positive weights. [41]
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm is the most suitable for finding the shortest route in a city map represented as a weighted graph with positive weights. It systematically explores the graph to find the shortest path from a source node to all other nodes, making it perfect for navigation applications where edge weights represent distance or travel time. [41]

questions.question: In an operating system, a situation arises where two or more processes are blocked forever, each waiting for a resource held by another process in the same set. What is this situation called, and which conditions must be met for it to occur?
feedbacks: Starvation is a situation where a process is indefinitely postponed, but it is not the same as a deadlock. [20]
This is the correct term for the situation where processes are stuck waiting for each other in a circular chain. [20]
This is a necessary condition for deadlock, where at least one resource must be held in a non-sharable mode. [20]
This is a necessary condition for deadlock, where a process holds at least one resource while waiting for another. [20]
This is a necessary condition for deadlock, where a resource cannot be forcibly taken from a process holding it. [20]
This is a necessary condition for deadlock, where a set of waiting processes must exist in a circular chain. [20]
questions.explanation: This situation is called a deadlock. For a deadlock to occur, four necessary conditions, known as the Coffman conditions, must be met simultaneously: Mutual Exclusion (resources cannot be shared), Hold and Wait (a process holds a resource while waiting for another), No Preemption (resources cannot be forcibly taken), and Circular Wait (a circular chain of processes waiting for resources held by the next process in the chain). [20]

questions.question: A financial application is processing a transaction that involves transferring money from a savings account to a checking account. This operation must be atomic. If the system crashes after debiting the savings account but before crediting the checking account, the database must roll back the debit. Which ACID property ensures this?
feedbacks: This is the correct answer. Atomicity guarantees that all operations within a transaction are completed as a single, indivisible unit. If any part fails, the entire transaction is rolled back. [34]
Consistency ensures that the transaction brings the database from one valid state to another, which is a result of atomicity in this case. [34]
Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. [34]
Durability ensures that once a transaction is committed, it remains committed even if the system fails. [34]
Normalization is a database design principle to reduce redundancy, not a transactional property.
Scalability refers to the system's ability to handle increased load.
questions.explanation: The Atomicity property of ACID transactions ensures that the money transfer operation is treated as an all-or-nothing affair. If the entire sequence of operations (debit from savings, credit to checking) cannot be completed successfully due to a system crash or any other error, the transaction is aborted, and any changes made, like the initial debit, are automatically rolled back. This prevents the database from being left in an inconsistent state. [34]

questions.question: A web developer wants to protect their application's user input forms from SQL injection attacks. The application uses a database to store user data. Which of the following is the most effective technique to prevent this type of attack?
answers: Validating user input on the client-side using JavaScript.
Using prepared statements with parameterized queries.
Encoding user input before storing it in the database.
Limiting the length of user input fields.
Hiding database error messages from the user.
feedbacks: Client-side validation is easily bypassed and should not be relied upon for security.
This is the correct answer. Prepared statements separate the SQL code from the data, making it impossible for an attacker to inject malicious SQL. [10, 16]
While encoding can help prevent some attacks like XSS, it is not the primary defense against SQL injection.
Limiting input length can be a minor hurdle for an attacker but does not prevent SQL injection.
While good practice for security, hiding error messages does not prevent the injection attack itself from being executed.
A WAF can help filter malicious requests, but secure coding practices like using prepared statements are the fundamental and most effective defense.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks is to use prepared statements with parameterized queries. This approach ensures that user-supplied input is always treated as data and never as executable SQL code. The database driver handles the proper escaping of the input, which effectively neutralizes any attempt to inject malicious SQL commands. [10, 16]

questions.question: A developer is creating a drawing application. The application has a base class 'Shape' with a method 'draw()'. It also has several derived classes like 'Circle', 'Rectangle', and 'Triangle', each with its own implementation of the 'draw()' method. The application can treat objects of these derived classes as objects of the base 'Shape' class and call the 'draw()' method, which will execute the specific implementation for that shape. What is this object-oriented programming concept called?
feedbacks: Encapsulation is the bundling of data with the methods that operate on that data.
Inheritance is the mechanism by which one class acquires the properties of another, which is used here, but the concept described is polymorphism.

This is the correct answer. Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass, and the correct method implementation is called at runtime based on the actual object type.
Abstraction involves hiding complex implementation details and showing only the essential features of the object.
Composition is a design principle where a class contains an object of another class.
Aggregation is a specialized form of association where an object 'has-an' another object.
questions.explanation: This concept is called polymorphism, which means 'many forms'. It allows a single interface (the 'draw()' method in the 'Shape' base class) to represent different underlying forms (the specific implementations in 'Circle', 'Rectangle', etc.). This enables the program to process objects of different classes through a single, uniform interface, making the code more flexible and extensible.

questions.question: A company is deploying a new application in a public cloud using an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) model. According to the shared responsibility model, which of the following is the company responsible for securing and managing?
answers: The physical security of the data center.
The operating system of the virtual servers.
The network configuration and firewall rules for their virtual network.
The underlying physical servers and storage hardware.
feedbacks: The cloud provider is responsible for the physical security of their data centers. [40]
The cloud provider manages the underlying virtualization infrastructure. [40]
In IaaS, the customer is responsible for patching and securing the guest operating system. [40]
The customer is responsible for configuring their virtual network, including firewall rules, to control traffic to their applications. [40]
The customer is always responsible for securing their own application code and data. [40]
The cloud provider is responsible for managing and maintaining the physical hardware. [40]
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model for Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), the cloud provider is responsible for the security *of* the cloud (i.e., the physical infrastructure, network, and hypervisor). The customer is responsible for security *in* the cloud. This includes managing and securing the guest operating system, configuring network controls like firewalls, and securing their own applications and data that run on the IaaS platform. [40]

questions.question: A software development team has completed the coding and unit testing phase of a new module. They now need to combine the module with other existing modules and test them as a group to ensure they work together correctly. What is this phase of testing called?
feedbacks: Unit testing involves testing individual components or modules in isolation. [31]
This is the correct answer. Integration testing is the phase where individual software modules are combined and tested as a group. [31, 37]
System testing involves testing the complete and integrated software system to evaluate its compliance with the specified requirements. [31]
Acceptance testing is performed by the end-users to determine if the system meets their requirements and is ready for delivery. [31, 37]
Regression testing is done to ensure that new code changes have not adversely affected existing features.
Alpha testing is a type of acceptance testing performed by internal teams before the product is released to external users. [37]
questions.explanation: This phase is called integration testing. The primary purpose of integration testing is to expose faults in the interaction between integrated units. After individual modules have been unit tested, they are combined, and integration testing is performed to verify that they function together as expected and that data flows correctly between them. [31, 37]

questions.question: A user types 'www.geeksforgeeks.org' into their web browser and presses Enter. The browser needs to find the IP address associated with this domain name to establish a connection. Which network service or protocol is responsible for translating the human-readable domain name into a machine-readable IP address?
feedbacks: HTTP is the application protocol used for transmitting web pages, but it relies on an IP address to establish the connection.
DHCP is used to automatically assign an IP address to a device on a network, not to resolve domain names.

This is the correct answer. DNS is the hierarchical and decentralized naming system for computers, services, or other resources connected to the Internet or a private network. It translates domain names to IP addresses. [1, 24]
ARP is used to resolve an IP address to a physical MAC address on a local network.
TCP is a transport layer protocol that provides reliable communication, but it operates with IP addresses, which must be resolved first.
FTP is an application protocol used for transferring files between a client and a server.
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) is responsible for this translation. Often referred to as the 'phonebook of the Internet', DNS resolves human-friendly domain names (like 'www.geeksforgeeks.org') into the numerical IP addresses (like '172.67.143.204') that computers use to identify each other on the network. This process is a fundamental step before any web browser can establish a connection to a web server. [1, 24]

questions.question: A data scientist has trained a complex machine learning model that performs exceptionally well on the training data but poorly on new, unseen data. What is this phenomenon called, and what are potential ways to mitigate it?
answers: Increase the complexity of the model.
Use a larger and more diverse training dataset.
Use regularization techniques (e.g., L1 or L2).
Train the model for more epochs.
feedbacks: Underfitting is when the model is too simple and performs poorly on both the training and test data. [49]
This is the correct term for when a model learns the training data too well, including its noise, and fails to generalize to new data. [49]
Increasing the model's complexity would likely worsen the overfitting.
A larger and more diverse dataset can help the model learn the underlying patterns better and generalize well. [49]
Regularization adds a penalty for model complexity, discouraging the model from fitting the noise in the training data and thus reducing overfitting. [49]
Training for too many epochs can lead to overfitting, so this would likely make the problem worse.
questions.explanation: This phenomenon is called overfitting. It occurs when a machine learning model becomes too closely tailored to the training data and loses its ability to generalize to new data. [49] Effective techniques to mitigate overfitting include training the model on a larger and more diverse dataset, and using regularization methods like L1 or L2, which penalize complex models and encourage them to learn simpler, more generalizable patterns. [49]

questions.question: A programmer is choosing between an array and a linked list to store a collection of elements. The application will involve frequent insertions and deletions of elements at arbitrary positions within the collection. Which data structure is generally more efficient for these specific operations and why?
answers: Array, because elements are stored in contiguous memory locations.
Linked List, because it only requires updating a few pointers to insert or delete an element.
Array, because it provides constant-time (O(1)) access to any element by its index.
Linked List, because it consumes less memory than an array.
Both are equally efficient for these operations.
A hash table would be the best choice.
feedbacks: The contiguous memory of an array makes insertions and deletions in the middle of the collection inefficient, as it requires shifting subsequent elements. [4]

This is the correct answer. Insertions and deletions in a linked list are efficient (O(1)) once the position is found, as it only involves changing the 'next' and 'previous' pointers of the adjacent nodes. [4]
While arrays have O(1) random access, this advantage does not apply to the efficiency of insertions and deletions.
A linked list typically consumes more memory than an array for the same number of elements due to the overhead of storing pointers for each node.
There is a significant performance difference between arrays and linked lists for insertions and deletions at arbitrary positions.
A hash table is not an ordered collection and is not suitable for insertions/deletions at specific positions in a sequence.
questions.explanation: For frequent insertions and deletions at arbitrary positions, a linked list is generally more efficient than an array. In an array, these operations require shifting all subsequent elements, resulting in a time complexity of O(n). In contrast, a linked list only requires updating the pointers of the adjacent nodes, which is a constant-time operation (O(1)) once the target location has been reached. [4]

questions.question: A system with multiple concurrent threads needs to control access to a limited pool of 10 database connections. A mechanism is required to allow a thread to acquire a connection if one is available and wait if all 10 are in use. Another thread can then release a connection back to the pool, allowing a waiting thread to proceed. Which synchronization primitive is best suited for this scenario?
feedbacks: A mutex allows only one thread to access a resource at a time, making it unsuitable for managing a pool of 10 connections. [30, 32]
This is the correct answer. A counting semaphore, initialized to 10, can manage access to the pool, allowing up to 10 threads to acquire a connection simultaneously. [30, 32]
A spinlock would cause waiting threads to waste CPU cycles by continuously polling, which is inefficient for potentially long waits like database connection availability.
A condition variable could be used with a mutex to build this, but a semaphore is a higher-level primitive that directly models this exact problem of managing a pool of N resources.
A read/write lock is for scenarios with many readers and few writers, not for managing a pool of identical, interchangeable resources.
An atomic counter could track the number of used connections, but it doesn't provide a mechanism for threads to wait when the pool is empty.
questions.explanation: A counting semaphore is the ideal synchronization primitive for managing a pool of a finite number of resources. By initializing the semaphore's count to the number of available resources (in this case, 10), it allows that many threads to acquire a 'permit'. When a thread needs a connection, it waits on the semaphore (decrementing the count). When a thread releases a connection, it signals the semaphore (incrementing the count), allowing another waiting thread to proceed. [30, 32]

questions.question: A database for a large e-commerce site needs to be indexed to provide very fast lookups for specific product IDs and also efficient retrieval of products within a certain price range. Which data structure is most commonly used for database indexing to satisfy both of these requirements effectively?
feedbacks: A hash table provides very fast lookups for individual keys but is not efficient for range queries, as it does not store keys in a sorted order.
This is the correct answer. B+ Trees store all data pointers in leaf nodes which are linked together, allowing for efficient range queries as well as fast individual lookups. [12, 36, 38]
A standard BST can become unbalanced, leading to poor performance (O(n)). While balanced BSTs exist, B+ Trees are optimized for disk-based storage systems.
An array would require a linear scan for lookups unless it's sorted, and insertions/deletions would be slow.
A heap is a priority queue and is not designed for efficient searching or range queries.
A trie is specialized for string-based keys and prefix searches, not for general-purpose database indexing of numerical IDs and ranges.
questions.explanation: B+ Trees are the most widely used data structure for indexing in relational database systems because they are optimized for disk-based storage and support both fast point queries and range queries. All data records or pointers are stored at the leaf level, and these leaf nodes are connected in a linked list. This structure allows for efficient sequential traversal, which is ideal for executing range-based searches. [12, 36, 38]

questions.question: An attacker on a local Wi-Fi network wants to intercept the traffic between a victim's computer and the network's router. The attacker sends forged network packets to both the victim and the router, falsely claiming that the attacker's MAC address corresponds to the other's IP address. As a result, all traffic between the victim and router is sent through the attacker's machine. What is this attack called?
feedbacks: DNS spoofing involves corrupting DNS cache data to redirect traffic to a malicious server, operating at a higher network layer.

This is the correct answer. The attack involves sending falsified ARP messages to link an attacker's MAC address with the IP address of a legitimate computer or server on a local network. [10, 11, 13]
IP spoofing involves creating IP packets with a forged source IP address to impersonate another system, but it doesn't inherently reroute traffic like ARP spoofing does.
Session hijacking is the result of a successful attack like ARP spoofing, where the attacker steals a valid session token, but it is not the initial network attack itself. [11]
While ARP spoofing can be used to cause a DoS, its primary purpose in this scenario is to intercept traffic for a man-in-the-middle attack. [10, 11]
MAC flooding is an attack on a network switch, overwhelming its MAC address table to make it act like a hub, not a targeted redirection of traffic.
questions.explanation: This attack is known as ARP Spoofing or ARP Cache Poisoning. It exploits the stateless nature of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) used on local networks to map IP addresses to physical MAC addresses. By sending unsolicited, forged ARP replies, the attacker tricks the victim's computer and the router into updating their ARP caches with the attacker's MAC address. This positions the attacker as a man-in-the-middle, allowing them to intercept, inspect, or modify all communication. [10, 11, 13]

questions.question: A distributed database system for a global e-commerce platform must remain operational and continue to accept orders even if a network failure temporarily severs the connection between its data centers in North America and Europe. However, this means that for a short period, inventory data might be inconsistent between the two regions. According to the CAP theorem, which two properties is this system prioritizing?
feedbacks: The system is sacrificing consistency, as the inventory data can be different in the two regions during the partition. [24, 35]
The system is prioritizing availability because it continues to accept orders (remains operational) in both regions despite the network failure. [24, 35]
The system is prioritizing partition tolerance because it is designed to continue operating even when there is a network partition between its data centers. [24, 35]
Durability is an ACID property related to committed transactions, not a direct component of the CAP theorem.
Isolation is an ACID property related to concurrent transactions, not a direct component of the CAP theorem.
Atomicity is an ACID property related to the all-or-nothing nature of transactions, not a direct component of the CAP theorem.
questions.explanation: According to the CAP theorem, a distributed system can only guarantee two of the following three properties at the same time: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. Since network partitions are a fact of life in distributed systems, the real choice is between consistency and availability. In this scenario, the e-commerce platform chooses to remain available for users in both regions during a network failure, thus prioritizing Availability and Partition Tolerance at the temporary expense of strong Consistency. [24, 35]

questions.question: A developer is working with a legacy charting library that has a complex and cumbersome interface. To simplify the interaction with this library for other parts of the application, the developer creates a new class that provides a simple, high-level interface for creating charts (e.g., `createPieChart(data)`). Deals with partial dependencies on composite keys.
3NF eliminates transitive dependencies.
A stricter version of 3NF.
Deals with multi valued dependencies.
The highest form rarely used in practice.

TCP is the transport protocol used by HTTP and DNS but DNS lookup comes first.
The Domain Name System is used to resolve names to IPs.

ARP resolves IPs to MAC addresses on a local network.
TLS secures the connection after the TCP handshake to the IP.

Short jobs get stuck behind long jobs.

A process repeatedly checks a condition instead of blocking.
questions.explanation: Priority inversion occurs when a high priority task is blocked by a lower priority task which can be solved with techniques like priority inheritance see operating systems concepts and GeeksforGeeks priority inversion.

questions.question: Which of the following data structures provides the fastest average-case time complexity for searching for an element?
feedbacks: A sorted array allows for O(log n) search using binary search.
A linked list requires an O(n) scan to find an element.
A Hash Table provides O(1) average-case time complexity for search operations.
A balanced BST provides O(log n) search time.
questions.explanation: A Hash Table uses a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets from which the desired value can be found in average constant time making it the fastest option.

questions.question: In an operating system what is a 'critical section'?
answers: The part of the operating system kernel that can never be modified.
A segment of code that accesses shared resources and which must not be concurrently executed by more than one thread or process.
The initial block of memory allocated to a process when it starts.
A special high-priority process that is never interrupted.
feedbacks: This is incorrect; a critical section is a concept in application code not the kernel's structure.
This is the correct definition. Access to a critical section is controlled by synchronization primitives to prevent race conditions.
This is part of the process's memory space but is not the definition of a critical section.
This is a hypothetical process type not the definition of a critical section.
questions.explanation: A critical section is a piece of code that must be executed atomically by only one thread at a time to ensure the integrity of shared data.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE in SQL? Select all that apply.
answers: DELETE is a DML command while TRUNCATE is a DDL command
TRUNCATE is faster than DELETE for removing all rows from a large table
DELETE can be used with a WHERE clause to remove specific rows but TRUNCATE removes all rows
DELETE operations can be rolled back in a transaction while TRUNCATE operations often cannot be
TRUNCATE resets identity columns back to their seed value but DELETE does not
feedbacks: This is a key distinction. DELETE manipulates data while TRUNCATE redefines the table's data content.
TRUNCATE is a minimally logged operation that deallocates data pages making it much faster than the row-by-row logged DELETE operation.
TRUNCATE does not accept a WHERE clause.
DELETE is a fully logged operation that can be undone whereas TRUNCATE is often a non-transactional or minimally logged command.
After a TRUNCATE an identity column will start from its initial value again.
questions.explanation: The main differences are that DELETE is a logged row-by-row DML operation that can be filtered with WHERE while TRUNCATE is a faster minimally logged DDL operation that removes all rows and resets table identities.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)?
answers: To carry user data for applications like web browsing.
To send error messages and operational information indicating success or failure when communicating with another IP address.
To resolve domain names into IP addresses.

This is typically handled by TCP or UDP.
ICMP is a network layer protocol used by network devices to diagnose communication issues. It is used by utilities like ping and traceroute.
This is the function of DNS (Domain Name System).
questions.explanation: ICMP is a supporting protocol in the Internet protocol suite used by network devices like routers to send error messages and operational information for example a requested service is not available or that a host or router could not be reached.

questions.question: In JavaScript what is the key difference between null and undefined?
answers: null is an object while undefined is a primitive type.
A variable is undefined when it has been declared but not assigned a value while null is an intentional assignment value representing 'no value'.
undefined means a variable does not exist while null means it exists but is empty.
There is no practical difference and they can be used interchangeably.

A variable that does not exist would throw a ReferenceError. undefined means it exists but has no value yet.
This is a common source of bugs. They are not interchangeable and represent different concepts.

questions.question: In cryptography what is the fundamental difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
answers: Symmetric encryption uses a single shared key for both encryption and decryption while asymmetric encryption uses a pair of keys (a public key and a private key).
Symmetric encryption is more secure than asymmetric encryption.
Symmetric encryption is a modern algorithm while asymmetric is outdated.
Symmetric encryption can only be implemented in hardware while asymmetric is software-only.
feedbacks: This is the core distinction. Asymmetric encryption uses a public key for encryption and a separate private key for decryption.
Asymmetric encryption is generally considered more secure for key exchange as the private key is never shared.
Both are modern and have different use cases. Symmetric is faster while asymmetric is better for secure key exchange.
Both can be implemented in either hardware or software.
questions.explanation: The primary difference lies in the keys used. Symmetric cryptography relies on a single shared secret key while asymmetric cryptography uses a public key available to anyone and a private key kept secret by the owner.

questions.question: Under which of the following conditions would a Linked List be a more suitable data structure than an Array? Select all that apply.
answers: The size of the collection is fixed and known in advance.
The application requires frequent and fast random access to elements by index.
The application requires frequent insertions and deletions of elements at the beginning or in the middle of the collection.
The collection of data is expected to grow and shrink frequently.
Memory locality and cache performance are critical.
feedbacks: Arrays are more memory-efficient for fixed-size collections.
Arrays provide O(1) random access which is much faster than the O(n) access of a linked list.
Linked lists excel at insertions and deletions in the middle (if the node is known) or at the ends as it only requires pointer manipulation (O(1)) not shifting elements (O(n)).
Linked lists are inherently dynamic and make it easy to add or remove elements as needed without pre-allocating a large block of memory.
Arrays have better memory locality as elements are stored contiguously which is better for CPU cache performance.
questions.explanation: A Linked List is preferable over an Array when the size of the collection is not known in advance and there will be a high number of insertions and deletions in the middle of the list which are O(1) operations for a linked list versus O(n) for an array.

questions.question: What is 'demand paging' in the context of virtual memory?
answers: The process of pre-loading all of a program's pages into memory before it starts executing.
The technique of loading a page into main memory only when it is needed or 'on demand'.
A memory allocation policy where the largest available block of memory is always chosen.
The process of an application demanding that its memory pages are never swapped out to disk.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of demand paging.
This is the correct definition. It means pages are only brought into RAM when a program tries to access them resulting in a page fault.
This describes a memory allocation algorithm not a paging strategy.
This would be memory pinning not demand paging.
questions.explanation: Demand paging is a virtual memory management technique where pages are loaded from secondary storage into main memory only when they are accessed by a process for the first time thereby reducing startup time and memory overhead.

questions.question: In a database transaction what is the purpose of the COMMIT statement?
answers: To undo all the changes made during the current transaction.
To save all the changes made during the current transaction making them permanent.
To create a savepoint within a transaction to which you can later roll back.
feedbacks: This is the function of the ROLLBACK statement.
The COMMIT statement concludes a transaction and makes all changes visible to other users and durable.
This is the function of the SAVEPOINT statement.
A new transaction is typically started implicitly after a COMMIT or explicitly with a BEGIN TRANSACTION statement.
questions.explanation: The COMMIT command is a transactional command used to save all the work done in a transaction to the database. It finalizes the transaction making its changes permanent.

questions.question: In IP networking what is the primary function of a subnet mask?
answers: To uniquely identify a device on a network.
To specify which part of an IP address represents the network and which part represents the host.
To translate a private IP address into a public IP address.
To automatically configure the IP address for a host.

A subnet mask is used to divide an IP address into two parts: one part identifies the network and the other identifies the host on that network.
This is the function of Network Address Translation (NAT).
This is the function of DHCP.
questions.explanation: A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that logically divides an IP address. The '1's in the subnet mask represent the network portion and the '0's represent the host portion allowing devices to determine if another IP address is on the same local network.

questions.question: What is the difference between passing a variable 'by value' and 'by reference' to a function?
answers: Pass-by-value sends the actual variable to the function while pass-by-reference sends a pointer.

When passing by value the function receives a copy of the variable's value and cannot modify the original variable. When passing by reference the function receives a reference to the original variable and can modify it.
Pass-by-reference is only used in object-oriented programming while pass-by-value is used in procedural programming.
There is no difference; they are just different terms for the same process.
feedbacks: This is a common implementation detail but the core concept is about copying vs. sharing.
This is the fundamental difference. Pass-by-value works on a local copy while pass-by-reference works on the original data.
Both paradigms can use either mechanism although some languages default to one over the other for certain data types.
They describe two fundamentally different ways of passing arguments to functions with very different outcomes.
questions.explanation: In pass-by-value the function gets a copy of the argument's value so the original argument is unchanged. In pass-by-reference the function gets a reference (or memory address) to the argument allowing it to modify the original variable.

questions.question: What is the 'Principle of Least Privilege' in computer security?
answers: The principle that security systems should be as simple as possible.
The principle that a user process or program should only have the minimum privileges necessary to perform its function.
The principle that the least secure part of a system determines its overall security.
The principle of giving administrators the fewest number of user accounts to manage.
feedbacks: While simplicity is a good design goal this is not the Principle of Least Privilege.
This is the correct definition. It limits the damage that can be caused by an error or a security breach.
This describes the concept of the 'weakest link' in security.
This is an administrative strategy not the Principle of Least Privilege.
questions.explanation: The Principle of Least Privilege is a fundamental concept in information security that states that any given user program or process should have only the bare minimum of permissions required to perform its task and nothing more.

questions.question: In a graph data structure how does a Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal differ from a Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal?
answers: DFS explores as deeply as possible along each branch before backtracking while BFS explores all of the neighbor nodes at the present depth prior to moving on to the nodes at the next depth level.
DFS uses a queue to keep track of nodes to visit while BFS uses a stack.
DFS is guaranteed to find the shortest path in an unweighted graph while BFS is not.
DFS is only for directed graphs while BFS is for undirected graphs.
feedbacks: This is the core difference in their traversal strategies. DFS goes deep; BFS goes wide.
This is the opposite. DFS is typically implemented with a stack (or recursion) and BFS is implemented with a queue.
This is the opposite. BFS is guaranteed to find the shortest path in an unweighted graph.
Both algorithms can be applied to both directed and undirected graphs.
questions.explanation: The fundamental difference is the exploration strategy: DFS explores a path to its conclusion before backtracking using a stack-like behavior whereas BFS explores all neighbors at one level before moving to the next using a queue-like behavior.

questions.question: In an operating system what is a hardware 'interrupt'?
answers: An error in a program that causes it to stop execution.
A signal to the processor emitted by hardware or software indicating an event that needs immediate attention.
A user command to interrupt a running process such as pressing Ctrl+C.
A period of time during which the CPU is idle and waiting for a task.
feedbacks: This is a software exception or a crash not a hardware interrupt.
This is the correct definition. An interrupt alerts the CPU to a high-priority event that requires interrupting the current code it is executing.
This is a type of software interrupt or signal generated by user input. The definition also includes hardware signals.
This is an idle state not an interrupt.
questions.explanation: An interrupt is a signal sent to the CPU that temporarily stops a running program and allows a special program an interrupt handler to run instead. This is used for I/O events timers and other critical system functions.

questions.question: What does a PRIMARY KEY constraint on a database table column ensure? Select all that apply.

It ensures that no value in the column can be NULL.
It automatically creates an index on the column to speed up queries.
It encrypts the data in the column.
It ensures the values in the column are sorted in ascending order.
It links the table to another table.
feedbacks: Uniqueness is a core property of a primary key. No two rows can have the same primary key value.
A primary key column cannot contain NULL values.
Database systems automatically create a unique index on the primary key column(s) to facilitate fast lookups.
Encryption is a separate security feature and not part of the primary key constraint.
While the index is sorted the physical storage of the table data is not guaranteed to be sorted by the primary key.
This is the role of a FOREIGN KEY not a primary key.
questions.explanation: A PRIMARY KEY is a special relational database table constraint that uniquely identifies each record in the table. It enforces both uniqueness and non-nullability and an index is automatically created on it.

questions.question: What is a 'cookie' in the context of web browsing?
answers: A small piece of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the web browser.
A script that runs on the user's browser to add interactivity to a web page.
An encrypted file that contains a user's password for a website.
A temporary file downloaded by the browser to store images and other assets for faster page loads.

This describes JavaScript not a cookie.
While a cookie can store a session identifier it should not store a password directly and is not inherently encrypted.
This describes the browser cache not a cookie.
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small block of data created by a web server while a user is browsing a website and placed on the user's computer or other device by the user’s web browser. It's used to remember information like session state or user preferences.

questions.question: In object-oriented programming what is the primary purpose of an 'interface'?
answers: To create an instance of an object.
To specify a contract of methods that a class must implement.
To hide the implementation details of a class.
To allow a class to inherit methods and properties from multiple superclasses.

This is a goal of abstraction and encapsulation. An interface contributes to this but its primary purpose is defining a contract.
While implementing multiple interfaces provides a form of multiple inheritance of type the primary purpose is to define a contract not to inherit implementation.
questions.explanation: An interface is a programming structure that acts as a contract by defining a set of methods that a class must implement. It allows for a powerful form of polymorphism and helps in designing loosely coupled systems.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'white-box' and a 'black-box' penetration test?
answers: White-box tests are performed by internal employees while black-box tests are performed by external consultants.
In a white-box test the tester is given full knowledge of the system including source code and architecture diagrams. In a black-box test the tester is given no prior knowledge of the system.
White-box testing is automated while black-box testing is done manually.
White-box testing focuses on network vulnerabilities while black-box testing focuses on application vulnerabilities.
feedbacks: The distinction is about knowledge not the tester's employment status.
This is the correct distinction. White-box testing simulates an attack from an insider with knowledge while black-box testing simulates an attack from an external hacker.
Both types of testing can use a combination of automated and manual techniques.
Both can be used to test either network or application layers.
questions.explanation: The key difference is the level of information provided to the tester. White-box (or clear-box) testing involves full knowledge of the target system while black-box testing involves no knowledge simulating an external attacker's perspective.

questions.question: A developer is implementing a recursive function. What is the most critical component that the function must have to avoid an infinite loop and a stack overflow error?
answers: A base case that stops the recursion.
feedbacks: A recursive function uses self-calls not loops to repeat.
A base case is a condition under which the function does not call itself again allowing the recursion to terminate and the call stack to unwind.
The type of parameter does not prevent infinite recursion.
While most recursive functions have a return value it is the base case that stops the recursion.
questions.explanation: Every recursive algorithm must have a base case which is a condition that is met to stop the recursion. Without a base case the function would call itself indefinitely leading to a stack overflow.

questions.question: In the context of CPU scheduling which algorithm can lead to 'starvation' for low-priority processes?
feedbacks: Round Robin is designed to be fair and prevent starvation by giving each process a time slice.
FCFS does not lead to starvation as every process will eventually be executed.
The non-preemptive version of SJN can cause long jobs to starve if short jobs keep arriving.
In a strict priority-based system a continuous stream of high-priority processes can prevent a low-priority process from ever getting the CPU.
questions.explanation: Starvation is a problem where a process is indefinitely postponed. This can happen in priority-based scheduling algorithms where a process with a low priority is always preempted by newly arriving high-priority processes.

questions.question: What is a 'database view' and what is its primary purpose?
answers: A physical copy of a table used for backup.
A named query that is stored in the database as a virtual table. Its purpose is to simplify complex queries and to restrict access to data.
An index used to speed up queries on a table.
A log of all transactions that have occurred in the database.
feedbacks: A view is a virtual table not a physical copy. It does not store data itself.
This is the correct definition. Views can be used to encapsulate complex joins and calculations and to provide a security layer by exposing only certain rows or columns.
This describes an index not a view.
This is a transaction log not a view.
questions.explanation: A database view is a searchable object in a database that is defined by a query. Though a view doesn't store data it can be queried as if it were a real table. This is used to simplify data access and enhance security.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets across multiple networks and uses logical addressing (like IP addresses)?
feedbacks: The Data Link Layer is responsible for node-to-node data transfer on the same local network and uses physical addresses (MAC addresses).
The Network Layer is responsible for packet forwarding including routing through intermediate routers. It uses logical addresses to identify hosts.
The Transport Layer provides host-to-host communication services for applications but does not handle routing between networks.
The Application Layer is the top layer where network-aware applications operate.
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for determining the best path for data to travel from source to destination across different networks a process known as routing. It uses logical addresses like IP addresses for this purpose.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'this' keyword (or 'self' in some languages) in object-oriented programming?
answers: To create a new instance of a class.
To refer to the current instance of the class within one of its own methods.
To call a method from the parent class.
To declare a variable that is shared among all instances of a class.
feedbacks: The 'new' keyword is used for creating new instances.
'this' is a reference to the current object allowing you to access its members (fields and methods) and to distinguish between instance variables and local variables with the same name.
The 'super' or 'base' keyword is used for this purpose.
The 'static' keyword is used to declare such a variable.
questions.explanation: In object-oriented programming 'this' (or 'self') is a keyword that refers to the specific instance of the object on which a method is being called. It is used to access instance variables and methods.

questions.question: What is 'salting' in the context of password hashing?
answers: Encrypting the password before hashing it.
Adding a unique random value to each password before it is hashed.
Using a slow hash function to make brute-force attacks more difficult.
Storing password hashes in a separate highly secure database.
feedbacks: Hashing is a one-way function; encryption is two-way. Salting is a specific technique applied during hashing.
This is the correct definition. A salt is combined with the password before hashing so that even if two users have the same password the resulting hashes will be different.
This is called key stretching. While often used with salting it is a separate concept.
This is a good security practice (a 'vault') but it is not what salting is.
questions.explanation: A salt is a unique randomly generated string that is added to each user's password before it is hashed. Salting prevents attackers from using precomputed rainbow tables to crack passwords and ensures that identical passwords hash to different values.

questions.question: A developer needs to find the longest palindromic substring within a given string. For example in 'babad' the longest palindromic substrings are 'bab' and 'aba'. Which algorithmic approach is often used to solve this efficiently?
feedbacks: A greedy approach of picking the longest palindrome at each step will not necessarily yield the globally longest one.
This is an efficient approach where you iterate through each character (and space between characters) as a potential center of a palindrome and expand outwards. This gives an O(n^2) solution.
While it can be solved this way it is generally more complex to implement than the expand from center or dynamic programming approaches.
Checking every possible substring for being a palindrome would be O(n^3) which is very inefficient.
questions.explanation: The 'Expand from Center' algorithm is an intuitive and efficient O(n^2) method for finding the longest palindromic substring. It iterates through all possible centers of a palindrome and expands outwards to find the longest palindrome for that center.

questions.question: What is the 'convoy effect' in the context of CPU scheduling?
answers: When a high-priority process is blocked by a low-priority process holding a required resource.
When several short processes get stuck waiting behind a single long CPU-bound process in a First-Come First-Served (FCFS) scheduler.
When the CPU is spending more time on context switching than on executing processes.
When all processes in the ready queue require the same I/O device.
feedbacks: This is priority inversion not the convoy effect.
This is the correct definition. The long process acts like a 'truck' at the front of a convoy holding up all the smaller 'cars' behind it leading to poor average waiting times.
This is high context switch overhead not the convoy effect.
This is a bottleneck on an I/O device not the specific CPU scheduling problem known as the convoy effect.
questions.explanation: The convoy effect is a performance issue in FCFS scheduling where a long-running process can monopolize the CPU forcing many shorter processes to wait for a long time significantly degrading the average response time.

questions.question: Which type of SQL join returns all rows when there is a match in either the left or the right table including non-matching rows from both sides?
feedbacks: An INNER JOIN only returns rows that have matching values in both tables.
A LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and only the matched rows from the right table.
A RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and only the matched rows from the left table.
A FULL OUTER JOIN combines the results of both LEFT and RIGHT joins. It returns all records from both tables and fills in NULL for missing matches on either side.
questions.explanation: A FULL OUTER JOIN is used when you want to retrieve all records from both tables involved in the join regardless of whether there is a match in the other table. It effectively combines a LEFT JOIN and a RIGHT JOIN.

questions.question: In the context of the OSI model which layer is responsible for the reliable transmission of data segments between two hosts including functions like flow control error checking and sequencing?
feedbacks: The Data Link Layer handles error control for its local link but the end-to-end reliability is handled at a higher layer.
The Network Layer (IP) is an unreliable best-effort delivery protocol; it does not guarantee delivery.
